html:
November 5, 2026

Democrats sweep midterms in historic landslide

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews, @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the Nov. 3 midterms, taking the national House popular vote by roughly 13 points and tracking toward about 258 seats, the party's largest House win since 1974. Turnout was the second-highest for a midterm in over a century and about 94% of counties shifted left, with every age group under 65, every major racial group and independents moving toward Democrats. Voters named government corruption (90%), cost of living (89%), the Iran war (74%) and immigration enforcement (73%) as crucial factors. Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis called the result close to an extinction-level event for Republicans, and Democrats flipped Republican-held Senate seats in Texas, South Carolina, Kansas, Iowa, Ohio, Maine and North Carolina.

Democrats flip Texas statewide and in the legislature

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews, @aaronparnas

Democrat James Talarico defeated Republican Ken Paxton for a US Senate seat, becoming the first Democrat elected to the Texas Senate delegation since 1988, in a race that drew more than $500 million in spending including $158 million from Elon Musk backing Paxton. Gina Hinojosa defeated Gov. Greg Abbott to become the state's first Latina governor. Democrats also flipped the Texas state House of Representatives and the state Board of Education. Don Huffines, whose family bought Jeffrey Epstein's Zorro Ranch, lost his race.

Democrats prepare sweeping investigations of Trump administration and corporate America

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Rep. Robert Garcia, the incoming chair of the House Oversight Committee, said no one named Trump is off limits in planned investigations, including the president, his children and his wife, along with ICE agents and officials. He also said he wants public hearings on the Epstein files and justice for survivors, and corporate executives accused of price gouging under oath. Separately, Democrats are preparing investigations across banking, insurance, media, healthcare, transportation, energy, manufacturing and trade, with companies that funded the White House ballroom reported to be near the top of the list. Rep. Steve Scalise circulated a letter telling Republican colleagues to take inventory of likely oversight targets, and Trump officials are reported to be struggling to retain enough law firms to represent them.

House moves to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth

tags: politics, defence
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual, @total.hypocrisy

Rep. Thomas Massie is expected to call up articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth as soon as next week, with the vote expected to pass with bipartisan support. Hegseth released a video saying "We will not back down," calling the impeachment push a sham and defending the Iran campaign, which he described as a historic battlefield victory. Trump praised Hegseth as having done a fantastic job, though CBS News reported the president has been asking advisers whether Hegseth should remain in the post after the midterm losses.

Trump allies break ranks as president is cast as a lame duck

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @ericmoutsos, @oafnation_actual

Trump said publicly that he was not on the ballot and would have won in a landslide if he had been, and told Politico the Iran war drove up gasoline prices in the short term while defending the decision. The Wall Street Journal reported he has largely disengaged from domestic issues to focus on foreign policy and his legacy, and he cancelled public events after the results. Marjorie Taylor Greene called for expelling him from the Republican Party, and Vice President JD Vance posted an analysis blaming the losses on the war, cost of living and the US relationship with Israel without clearing it with the White House. Marco Rubio is expected to leave the administration to launch a presidential bid, according to a report in The Independent.

Trump orders rollback of ICE operations after deportations touched his circle

tags: immigration, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Trump confronted Stephen Miller over immigration enforcement and directed that deportation operations be scaled back, according to the Wall Street Journal. The intervention followed Melania Trump telling her husband that she personally knew people who were being deported and that the campaign had gone too far.

North Carolina Republican gerrymander backfires as Democrats lead 10 of 14 seats

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews

Democrats are on track to flip six Republican-held congressional seats in North Carolina, reversing a redistricting plan designed to produce an 11-3 Republican advantage. Republicans spread their voters too thinly, leaving many districts with narrow margins that fell to the Democratic wave. Among the defeated are Richard Hudson, chairman of the National Republican Congressional Committee, and former state House Speaker Tim Moore. Two districts remain uncalled, with margins of 99 and 233 votes that could trigger recounts.

Voters decide billionaire tax, voter ID and transgender sports measures

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews

Montana approved I-194 barring corporate, union and some nonprofit election spending, an approach designed to challenge Citizens United. Nevada, North Carolina and Ohio approved photo voter ID requirements while California rejected Prop 39's ID mandate, and California's Prop 40 billionaire wealth tax trailed 56% to 44% in an uncalled race. Idaho voters rejected Prop 1, which would have replaced the state's near-total abortion ban with abortion rights up to viability, and Massachusetts rejected repealing recreational marijuana sales. Measures restricting transgender participation in school sports were leading in Washington and Colorado, and Florida approved a fivefold increase in its homestead exemption that could cost local governments about $5 billion in the first year.

State governments flip to Democrats across the country

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews, @aaronparnas

Democrats gained trifectas in Michigan, Minnesota, Nevada, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin, bringing them to 21 state trifectas against 18 for Republicans, with Arizona uncalled and leaning Democratic. Democratic governorships rose to 28 of 50, with Alaska and Kansas still uncalled. Georgia, Iowa, New Hampshire, North Carolina, Ohio and Texas moved out of single-party Republican control into divided government. Thirty-six states saw no change in party control.

Nasdaq falls into correction on fears of AI data center restrictions

tags: markets, tech
sources: @groundnews

US equities dropped sharply as investors anticipated that Democratic control of Congress would bring restrictions on building the computing facilities that support artificial intelligence. The Nasdaq slid 5.5% into correction territory, more than 10% below its October peak, while the Dow lost 1,833 points, or 3.4%, and the S&P 500 fell 4.4%. AI chip suppliers Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices lost 9.2% and 17.3% respectively.

Senate Democrats to probe JPMorgan's handling of Epstein accounts

tags: legal, politics
sources: @groundnews

Senate Finance Committee staff plan to examine JPMorgan Chase's banking relationship with Jeffrey Epstein when Democrats take control of the chamber in January, including decisions by asset and wealth management head Mary Callahan Erdoes. Sen. Ron Wyden, the committee's expected next chair, has pledged to use subpoena authority. A lawyer for the US Virgin Islands alleged in 2023 that the bank waited until after Epstein's death to report over $1 billion in suspicious transactions; Erdoes testified she knew in 2006 of allegations involving underage girls, and the bank kept him as a client until 2013. JPMorgan paid $290 million to victims and $75 million to settle the Virgin Islands suit and denies helping Epstein commit crimes.

Justice Department civil rights chief Harmeet Dhillon resigns

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

Harmeet Dhillon resigned as assistant attorney general for civil rights, the first senior Justice Department official to leave after the midterms. She took over the Civil Rights Division in April 2025 and reoriented it toward conservative causes, including ending school desegregation efforts in the South. More resignations are expected before the end of the year, and departing officials are not shielded from subpoenas.

Musk spent $445 million on federal races and faces congressional scrutiny

tags: politics, tech
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

Elon Musk spent about $445 million on federal races, according to Reuters, with just three of the 43 House Republicans he backed winning and six of his seven Senate picks losing. Rep. Robert Garcia said the entire Democratic caucus wants Musk to testify under oath over his role in cutting the federal workforce, handling of government data and his companies' federal contracts. Senate Democrats are also preparing an investigation into restrictions on Ukraine's military satellite communications and have told Musk to preserve documents, after SpaceX's Starshield service was slowed in October and degraded Ukrainian air defenses. Musk says the US government controls Starshield limits.

Paraguay president resigns after collapse of bank linked to him

tags: politics, markets
sources: @groundnews, @ericmoutsos

President Santiago Peña resigned after the collapse of Ueno Bank, a digital lender serving more than 60% of Paraguayan adults, saying the decision was for national stability and democratic institutions. The resignation followed impeachment threats from his own Colorado Party, protests with clashes with riot police, and the detention of eight bank executives. Peña held a stake in Ueno's holding company until last year and appointed a former Ueno executive to lead the central bank. The lender held roughly $800 million in public deposits before regulators seized it over financial irregularities, and accounts were frozen shortly after 3 a.m.

Israel certifies election as Netanyahu's bloc falls short of a majority

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews

Israel's Central Elections Committee certified the Oct. 27 results 15-14 after an audit of about 75% of polling stations found no evidence of irregularities. Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc won 53 of 120 Knesset seats, eight short of a majority, while Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc won 48 and Arab parties won a record 19. Likud had sought to delay certification over fraud allegations against Arab parties; committee chair Noam Sohlberg said challenges to the vote's integrity posed a real danger to Israeli democracy, and the attorney general rejected a Shin Bet request to question Arab lawmakers. President Isaac Herzog has 28 days, extendable by 14, to pick a leader to form a government, and both blocs have ruled out coalitions with Arab parties.

Russia agreed to supply Iran with 90 helicopter missile launchers

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Industry documents reviewed by the Financial Times list 90 APU-L launchers for a buyer coded K-10, identified as Iran. The launchers carry LMUR missiles, which Russia has used widely in Ukraine. The documents do not indicate whether the launchers were delivered.

World leaders read the US result as a signal on war and cost of living

tags: politics, foreign
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said Americans voted against policies that impoverish people and against hate and climate denial. Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Americans said no to war and endorsed the message, warning that betraying that public will would bring consequences. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the world now has an opportunity to unite around cost of living but that pressures cannot ease until the Middle East and Ukraine conflicts are resolved, and Israeli opposition leader Yair Golan said the results show how toxic Netanyahu has become in both US parties. Leaders in Russia, Poland, the Czech Republic, Norway, South Africa and Canada also responded.

Hegseth expands National Guard role in Washington DC

tags: politics, policing
sources: @oafnation_actual

A memo obtained by Politico shows Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth authorized National Guard troops in Washington to use boats, marked police cars, Humvees and tactical vehicles. Guard boats will support police operations in Anacostia. The DC deployment began in August 2025 under Trump's crime emergency.

Newsom commutes all 548 California death sentences

tags: legal, politics
sources: @groundnews

California Gov. Gavin Newsom announced he plans to commute the death sentences of all 548 inmates on the state's death row to life imprisonment without parole. About 60% of the commutations require California Supreme Court approval before his term ends in January. Newsom argued in a letter to Californians that capital punishment undermines justice and disproportionately affects people of color; the state has not executed anyone since 2006 and has been under a moratorium since 2019. The death penalty remains legal in California, so courts may still impose new death sentences.

Russell Brand convicted of rape and sexual assault

tags: legal
sources: @groundnews, @aaronparnas

Russell Brand was convicted at Southwark Crown Court in London of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault, and cleared of two further rape charges and one count of attempted indecent assault. The judge warned the 51-year-old that he should expect a custodial sentence, with sentencing to come later. Brand had denied every allegation, arguing the encounters were consensual or that his accusers had invented or recast events.

Judge pauses construction of Trump's Washington arch

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

A federal judge ordered construction of Trump's planned triumphal arch in Washington DC halted for at least two weeks. Judge Tanya Chutkan issued the pause following opposition from local activists and organizers in the DC area.

Trump designates Oval Office and cabinet room a national landmark

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Trump signed an executive order designating the Oval Office and the cabinet room a national landmark, aimed at preventing a future administration from undoing the gold decorative work he installed. An executive order can be reversed by any future president, and incoming presidents commonly revoke their predecessors' orders on taking office.

Democratic socialist Nithya Raman projected to unseat LA Mayor Karen Bass

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews

Decision Desk HQ projects city council member Nithya Raman defeating Mayor Karen Bass 51.1% to 48.33% in Los Angeles. Raman, born in Kerala, India, and a naturalized citizen, would be the first Asian American to lead the second-largest US city. She describes herself as both a capitalist and a democratic socialist, and campaigned on homelessness, rent and housing costs, tenant protections and public safety.

Poland arrests suspects accused of spying for Russia and supplying weapons parts

tags: legal, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Poland's Internal Security Agency said a group illegally sent Russia significant quantities of components used to produce ammunition and weapons systems. Reuters reported the suspects include five Poles and a 37-year-old Russian woman.

Boebert trails Democratic challenger in Colorado's 4th District

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews

Eileen Laubacher leads Lauren Boebert 49.18% to 47.70% with an estimated 87% of votes counted in Colorado's 4th Congressional District. Boebert carried the district by 11.6 points in 2024.

Undisclosed funding of political content creators draws congressional subpoenas

tags: media, politics
sources: @total.hypocrisy

Chorus, a network of nearly 200 political content creators co-founded by Stuart Perlmutter and Brian Tyler Cohen, pays creators who are not required to disclose that affiliation, while an affiliated for-profit agency, Good Influence, is paid by campaigns to commission content that appears organic. The House Oversight Committee sent document requests to the 1630 Fund in November 2025 and to Chorus's new nonprofit, the Creator Collective, in March 2026, receiving 135 and 62 pages respectively, with members calling the redactions obstructive. A subpoena issued to the 1630 Fund in May 2026 was complicated after Chorus shifted its funding away from that fund mid-investigation. FEC records show $10,000 from the AIPAC-backed campaign of Haley Stevens going to Good Influence; Aaron Parnas has confirmed receiving $24,000 from Chorus.

Utah voters urged to cure ballots as close races remain uncounted

tags: elections, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

Utah election results show Senate Majority Leader Kirk Cullimore, who was running to replace Stuart Adams as Senate president, likely out, and Amendment B, which would have given the legislature more power, defeated. Several races remain too close to call and final counts could take up to two weeks. Voters whose ballots were set aside over signature issues can respond to county clerk notices, and those who cast provisional ballots requiring ID face a deadline of close of business Monday, November 9.

Iowa Democrat who quit race wins seat anyway

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews

Democrat Eric Armstrong won an Iowa House seat despite ending his campaign in September over health problems, beating Republican Keith Jones by roughly 865 votes, a nine-point margin. The retired railroad executive succeeds Democrat Josh Turek, who won a US Senate seat. Armstrong said he will do his best to represent constituents but is still struggling with health issues.

19-year-old elected clerk of Maricopa County Superior Court

tags: politics, legal
sources: @groundnews

Arizona State University student Sebastian Matta, 19, won election to oversee court records in Maricopa County, the fourth most populous county in the nation. Republican opponent Jeff Dial, a former state senator, conceded by phone. Matta said he will spend his opening months building relationships with staff and assuring them their positions are secure, delaying proposed changes while he learns the role.

Fired Pentagon official flips Nancy Mace's seat

tags: politics, elections
sources: @oafnation_actual

Nancy LaCore, who was fired by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth without explanation, ran for Congress and flipped Nancy Mace's South Carolina seat to the Democrats.

Cyberattacks hit French blood banks

tags: health, tech
sources: @ericmoutsos

Cold-storage temperatures and defrosting thresholds were raised to very high levels at three French facilities holding vital blood products, destroying emergency blood stocks. The incident was described as the latest in a series of cyberattacks in Europe.
